script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'hail-b5b1-python',
  description: 'B5 part B1, the Python side: the summary module (the five-season table and the roof lines), the products additions (zone editions, kind words, events per tile), the site build and templates for the town and About pages, the contract rows, the docs and the job steps; four builders, three reviewers, skeptics, fixers, re-check',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Build', detail: 'products additions; summary module; site Python and templates; docs and job' },
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'data; rules and words; job and budget' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'one skeptic per finding' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'fixers by ownership' },
    { title: 'Recheck', detail: 'suite, builds, pages, record' },
  ],
}
const WT = '/home/user/wt/wt-b5'
const BASE = 'db84d76'
const BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b5-brief.md'
const B2BRIEF = '/home/user/wt/briefs/hail-b2-brief.md'
const RESEARCH = '/home/user/wt/research-b35'
const OUT = '/home/user/hail-b5/out'
const CACHE = '/home/user/hail-b5/cache'
const RECHECK = '/home/user/hail-b5/out/b5a-recheck-completion.json'
const STORE_TAR = '/home/user/hail-b2/out2/joins/hail-store.tar.gz'
const VENV = '/home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python'
const NORTH = `Product north star: one map; one sheet per place that leads with a plain summary; details behind headings in a fixed order; every number next to its unit and its kind word; nothing a roofer has to decode.`
const COMMON = `You work in the git worktree ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b5, based on ${BASE}; the part A data modules climate.py, stations.py, snowgrid.py, gauges.py and the joins.py extensions are in WIP commits). Read ${BRIEF} in full first: it is the contract, and its last two sections ("Supervisor decisions after the part A review (D17 to D26)" and "Supervisor decisions after the part A completion (D27 to D30) and the split of part B") are this run's rules and task list; a later decision wins over an earlier one. Then read the part A re-check ${RECHECK} (its contract_facts_part_b block holds the facts the site needs; its open_items_part_b is the gap list), the module docstrings of website/climate.py, website/stations.py, website/snowgrid.py, website/gauges.py and website/joins.py (their describe_*, map_data_* and WORDS_* are the public API), website/hail.py and website/build.py (the Collector, the --hail-history flag, the town pages and the About page), the B2 brief's data layout and words sections (${B2BRIEF}), and the research records under ${RESEARCH}/ your task names (roof-indicators.json and its refuter for the roof lines). ${NORTH} Repository rules (AGENTS.md is in your context): Python first (every word the viewer reads is written in Python), evidence honesty (kinds apart on every row; never damage, risk, probability, insurance, eligibility, all-clear; missing never zero; "Data unavailable" with the reason), feed contracts (a CONTRACTS row per source with units, timing, cadence and missing rules, changed with the parser and the tests), plain wording in sentence case, no em-dashes, no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names in repository files, tests with every behaviour change, no new pip package for the site build. This is part B1, the Python side: do not edit website/static/map/map.js, map.css or the sheet markup of map.html (part B2 builds the browser after B3 lands). Edit only the files you own (the OWNERSHIP map of this run); other builders edit other files in the same worktree now, so never run git checkout, stash, reset, add, commit or push, never reformat a file you do not own, and never delete anything outside a folder you created under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ (tests delete only folders they created). Disk is tight (about 3 GB free): the products builder makes one combined store at ${OUT}/b1/store from the B2 tar ${STORE_TAR} plus the part A modules (climate from the cached aggregates under ${CACHE}/nclimgrid, stations and gauges offline from ${CACHE}/, products offline from ${CACHE}/joins) and announces it by writing ${OUT}/b1/store-ready.json; every other builder reads that store and builds sites into ${OUT}/<your-name>/ one at a time, deleting each when its check is done. Caches are untrusted data (python -I for scripts that read them). A python with numpy, h5py, pyproj, pyogrio and Pillow is ${VENV}. Network is available for the zone editions only. Return a plain report: what you built (files, line counts), the measurements, the gate results you can show, and anything not done or needing a decision.`

const PRODUCTS2 = `${COMMON}

You are the products builder of part B1. You own website/joins.py, tests/test_joins.py, website/data/hail-fixture/ (its j/, z/, k/ and e/ files, index.json and manifest.json), and for D28 only the unavailable-block sentences of website/stations.py and website/gauges.py with their tests. Build: (1) D27: find the NWS public-zone shapefile archive of previous editions (the GIS page lists z_<ddmmmyy>.zip files with effective dates; make one listing request and check the content), fetch the editions whose effective dates cover 2021-10-17 to today into ${CACHE}/zones-editions/, place every zone-product event by the edition in force at its issue time, record per product how many events each edition placed and how many stay unplaced (expected 0; each remaining one listed with its code and date and a reason), and say in the zone words how many products could not be placed when the count is not zero; (2) D29: KIND_WORDS for every product code the store holds, by its NWS name, with a test that lists every code in the store and asserts a name; (3) D30: hail/j/e/<tile>.json per tile holding the events the tile's records reference (format hail-events-tile-v1; the same row shapes as events.json), written beside events.json; verify checks every referenced event is in its tile's file and records the largest file raw and gzip (budget 100 KB gzip); the index "joins" block names the format and the count; (4) B2's "in the window" phrases in the zone-product words and the wind zone contract facts reworded to "in these five years" with the tests that quote them; (5) the radar sentence and the hit-and-miss About sentence confirmed in WORDS_JOINS; (6) D28 in stations.py and gauges.py: the unavailable index blocks carry the D20 sentence beside the technical reason, with tests; (7) the fixture regenerated (keep it small; the k/ and e/ samples). Then build the combined store: tar -xzf ${STORE_TAR} into ${OUT}/b1/store, run the climate build from the cached aggregates, the stations and gauges builds offline, the snow build (its check fails by design, so n/ is absent and the index block says so), and the joins build offline with --procs 2 into that store; run every verify; write ${OUT}/b1/store-ready.json with the counts, sizes and the verify results; keep that store (every other builder reads it) and delete every other store copy you made. Report the D27 placement table, the largest e/ file, the kind-word list and the verify tails.`

const SUMMARY = `${COMMON}

You are the summary builder. You own website/summary.py (new) and tests/test_summary.py (new). Build summary.py: (1) the five-season table of the brief's Product section for a cell, from every store part (B1 hail days by class and the largest radar estimate with its date; B2 and B5 counts from the joins files: hail and wind reports within 5 miles, the largest reported hail with its date, warnings and zone products by kind, flood and freezing rain reports; station gust days and the strongest gust from s/; the climate counts and extremes from c/ (D19's rules, the highest and lowest with dates, freeze-thaw, lows below 32 F, highs of 90 F or more, precipitation and the largest one-day precipitation); the snow rows from sd/ (station readings: season snowfall and the deepest snow with its date; the analysis row absent because the D7 check failed, with the one About sentence of D23); the county products from k/; the gauge line from g/ for town pages only (D6)): each row a plain dict {label, kind, unit, values per season, five-season value, notes} with every value an integer or null and never a zero standing for missing; "Data unavailable" with the reason where a part or a season lacks data; the partial season line of D20 below the table; (2) the roof section: the 23 indicator lines of ${RESEARCH}/roof-indicators.json (its measurements.section_layout, templates and kind_words, as corrected by its refuter) grouped "Thresholds", "Snow and ice", "Wind and hail", "Heat and rain", "Lightning and sun", each a count or measurement with its kind word and one reference sentence per stressor quoting a public source named in that record (kind "Reference"; never a finding; never what a roof needs), and the held lines of D14 as "Data unavailable" with their reasons; WORDS_INDICATORS and the forbidden-term list of that record extended per D13; (3) describe_summary(store, row, col, now, town=None) returning the table and the sections' words for the town pages, and map_data_summary(index) returning the templates, the row order, the kind words and the units for the browser (part B2 fills them); (4) tests on a synthetic store the test writes (a few tiles of each part; every row kind; a season with missing months; a part that is unavailable; the forbidden terms; the partial season; no zero for missing). Wait for ${OUT}/b1/store-ready.json (poll every 3 minutes up to 90 minutes), then run describe_summary for the gate cell (row 797, column 1986), Benchland's cell and Billings, write the three tables to ${OUT}/summary/tables.json and read them as a roofer would: every cell a number with its unit and kind word, nothing to decode (gate B5-11's Python half); report what reads badly and fix it.`

const SITE = `${COMMON}

You are the site builder (Python side). You own website/build.py, website/sources.py, website/templates/town.html, website/templates/about.html, tests/test_site.py and tools/smoke_pages.py. The summary and products builders are writing website/summary.py and the joins.py additions now (poll every 3 minutes up to 90 minutes for summary.describe_summary, summary.map_data_summary and the e/ files before your integration tests; build the templates, the contract rows and the flag plumbing meanwhile). Build: (1) build.py: with --hail-history also copy hail/c, hail/sd, hail/g, hail/k and hail/j/e from the store (hail/n only when the index snow block says shown), include them in the manifest check, add map.json["hail"] blocks "climate", "snow", "stations", "gauges", "county" and "summary" from the map_data functions (the browser fills them in part B2), render the town pages with the summary table first (a <table> with scope headers, every cell a value with its unit, the kind word in the row label, "Data unavailable" cells with their reason in a footnote list) and the new sections in the brief's fixed order (Hail; Wind; Storms and warnings; Temperature; Rain; Snow; Flooding; Ice and winter; Heat; Weather that matters for a roof; How this was made), the town's gauge line (D6), the roof section, and the How-this-was-made block; the About page gains the new sources with their terms quoted exactly from the module docstrings (the contract facts), the D23 sentence that the snow analysis was checked against station totals and left out, the hit-and-miss sentence, the Census acknowledgement for the county file, the roof references; a store whose part is unavailable builds with the unavailable sentences; the flag-off build stays byte-identical to the base except shared static assets; a --hail-history build from a B2-only store (no c/, sd/, g/, k/) still builds with every new part unavailable; (2) sources.py: CONTRACTS rows nclimgrid_daily, nohrsc_season_snowfall, ghcn_daily, iem_watchwarn (the extended products with the period and polygon rules), iem_lsr (the extended types; the unverified magnitude codes not shown), nwps_gauges, usgs_water_api, census_counties and roof_references, each with units, timing, cadence and missing rules from the module docstrings and the brief's contract section, gated like hail_history, listed with the hail rows; (3) templates town.html and about.html; (4) tests/test_site.py: the flag plumbing and the new copies, the identity checks, the contract rows, the town page's table and sections in order from a fixture store the test writes (every row with a unit and a kind word; no zero for missing; the partial line; the unavailable cells), the About terms with the flag only; (5) tools/smoke_pages.py covers the town pages' table at 288 to 1440 px (no sideways scroll; the table reflows to one card per row at 390 px). Build and check: ${VENV} -m unittest tests.test_site (tail); builds from a copy of the worktree without .git: flag-off --sample --now 2026-10-19T12:00:00Z against the same build from the ${BASE} archive (diff -rq; only shared static assets may differ); --hail-history --sample into ${OUT}/site/sample; once ${OUT}/b1/store-ready.json exists, --hail-history --sample --hail-store <a tar of that store, or the folder if build.py takes one> into ${OUT}/site/real and run PW_CHROMIUM=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium ${VENV} tools/smoke_pages.py on it (tail); open the Billings and Benchland town pages' HTML and read the table as a roofer would; delete each build when checked. Report what you changed and measured.`

const DOCS = `${COMMON}

You are the docs and job builder. You own docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/DESIGN.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, README.md, AGENTS.md, research/hail-history/validation-evidence/b5-verification.json (new) and .github/workflows/hail-store.yml (the B5 steps only). Write D38 "The past weather of every location (B5, 2026-10-19)" after D35 (B3's D36 and B4's D37 are on their own branches; leave a one-line note that D36 and D37 arrive with those branches): the owner's request quoted once, the decisions it serves, the eight sources with their terms quoted exactly from the module docstrings and the brief (and the sources left out with reasons: FEMA flood zones, lightning strikes, PRISM, Daymet, SNODAS, SNOTEL), the grid-estimate and station-reading distinction, the thresholds of D1 and D19, the coverage rules of D5 and D18, the store layout, the backfill-once design and its asset, the period rule D8, the polygon rule D11 with the measured cover changes (B5-15 in ${RECHECK}), the zone editions D27, the events per tile D30, the snow analysis checked and left out (D7, D23: the slope 0.664 over 682 station-seasons), the summary table and why it leads the sheet (the north star), the roof section's basis, the hit-and-miss record (737 rows, 464 hits, 273 misses), the counsel items, the open owner decisions (O4 to O11 as ruled provisionally), and *Why:* in the house style. DESIGN.md section 12: the summary table (columns, units, kind words, the Data unavailable cell, the partial line), the sections and their states, the data contract additions (c/, sd/, g/, k/, j/e/, n/ when shown), the browser duties for part B2 (listed as pending). ROADMAP: the B5 row under Done with "measured in the re-check" where numbers are pending, the part B2 items, the open items (the gauge cut-off, the NOHRSC method, the LSR unit codes, the data-site split, the schedule cadence, the zone editions count). README and AGENTS: the modules in the layout, the job's steps, the flag. The verification record b5-verification.json with gates B5-1 to B5-18 filled from ${RECHECK} where part A settled them and pending otherwise. hail-store.yml: the B5 steps after the joins step under D26 (daily scope; the monthly steps behind a schedule or a manual input; the backfill once as a documented manual step with its asset; every step non-fatal with a timeout from the measured times in ${RECHECK} and the part A reports; no "=="; the YAML parses); measure nothing yourself: quote the records. Em-dashes 0; no model, AI-vendor or AI-product names; no invented measurements; quotes exact. Read the summary and site builders' words as they appear (poll every 5 minutes up to 90 minutes) so DESIGN matches. Report the diff stat.`

const FINDINGS = { type: 'object', properties: { findings: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, file: { type: 'string' }, line: { type: 'integer' }, claim: { type: 'string' }, evidence: { type: 'string' }, fix: { type: 'string' }, severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocking', 'should', 'minor'] }, confidence: { type: 'number' } }, required: ['id', 'file', 'line', 'claim', 'evidence', 'fix', 'severity', 'confidence'] } }, measurements: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: true }, gates: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { gate: { type: 'string' }, status: { type: 'string', enum: ['pass', 'fail', 'not_checked'] }, evidence: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['gate', 'status', 'evidence'] } }, summary: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['findings', 'measurements', 'gates', 'summary'] }
const VERDICT = { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, defect_real: { type: 'boolean' }, refuted: { type: 'boolean' }, severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocking', 'should', 'minor'] }, reason: { type: 'string' }, fix_ok: { type: 'boolean' }, adjusted_fix: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'defect_real', 'refuted', 'severity', 'reason', 'fix_ok', 'adjusted_fix'] }

const REVIEW_COMMON = `Read-only reviewer in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b5, based on ${BASE}). Read ${BRIEF} first (Product, rules D1 to D30, the store files, the words, the gates, the part B split: this run is part B1, the Python side; map.js, map.css and the sheet markup are part B2 and are not findings here), then ${RECHECK}. ${NORTH} The combined store is ${OUT}/b1/store (read it; never write into it); builders' reports are under ${OUT}/*/. Never edit, stage, commit or push; scratch only under ${OUT}/<your-name>/ which you create (disk is tight: one site build at a time, deleted when checked); never delete anything outside it. Report concrete defects only, each with file, line, evidence and an exact minimal fix; rank blocking first; a cell without a unit or a kind word, a zero standing for missing, or a sentence that needs decoding is a real finding; fill the gates you checked; put every measured number in measurements.`
const REVIEWERS = [
  { key: 'data', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: the numbers on the page. From the combined store and your own reads: (1) the summary table for the gate cell (row 797, column 1986), Benchland's cell and Billings: recompute at least six rows per place from the store files yourself (the hail days by class from t/, the report counts from j/, the climate counts and extremes from c/, the station snow and gusts from sd/ and s/, the warnings by kind) and compare with describe_summary's values (zero difference); every row has a unit and a kind word; no zero stands for missing; the partial line reads per D20; (2) D27: the zone editions placed the events the index records; pick ten events with old codes and confirm their placement edition by the effective dates; the unplaced count is zero or explained; (3) D29: every product code in the store has its NWS name in the words; (4) D30: for twenty tiles, every event the tile's records reference is in its e/ file and nothing else; the largest e/ file raw and gzip; (5) the town pages of Billings and Benchland built by the site builder: the table's values equal describe_summary's and the sections appear in the fixed order; the gauge line at Billings names BILM8 and its distance and is absent at Benchland; (6) the About page quotes the terms exactly as the module docstrings give them (diff the strings); (7) the D28 sentences in the stations and gauges blocks after an injected failure in your scratch.` },
  { key: 'rules', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: repository rules and words over the whole diff of part B1 (git -C ${WT} diff --stat, the full diff, untracked files; the part A WIP commits are the base of this review, so review only the working-tree changes plus summary.py). Check: Python first; evidence honesty (grep every new word for damage, damaged, risk, probability, chance, insurance, claim, coverage, eligible, confirmed, all clear, no hail, safe, structural, replace, repair, leak, loss, policy, warranty, expect outside quoted remarks, the allowed contexts of D13 and the "not the same as no hail" sentence; kinds apart on every row; "Data unavailable" never zero; one source per row; "Reference" lines never a finding); every CONTRACTS row matches its module docstring and the parser (units, cadences, missing rules, the unverified LSR unit codes not shown, the terms quotes exact); tests exist for every behaviour change and ${VENV} -m unittest discover -s tests passes (quote the tail) and python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload passes; the YAML of hail-store.yml parses, has no "==", and every B5 step is non-fatal with a timeout from a measured figure; the docs make no unmeasured claim and quote the re-check numbers exactly (D38, DESIGN 12, ROADMAP, README, AGENTS, b5-verification.json); em-dashes in added lines 0; the words Claude, Anthropic, Codex, ChatGPT, OpenAI, Copilot, Gemini, the worker model, the larger model, the mid model in added lines only inside branch names; plain wording and sentence case; no new pip package; decision 7 audit: every rmtree, unlink or os.remove under tests/ acts on a folder the test created; D4 audit; the flag-off identity (build both from a copy of the worktree and the ${BASE} archive; diff -rq).` },
  { key: 'job', prompt: `${REVIEW_COMMON} Lens: the job and the budget (gate B5-12). From the part A records and your own timed runs in your scratch (one store copy at a time): the daily sequence as hail-store.yml now runs it (B1 per the brief's 612 s figure, the joins step, the climate daily update, the station refresh under D26's daily scope, the NWPS refresh, the gauges, the pack) with its measured sum against the 25-minute budget and the 60-minute timeout; the monthly steps' sum; every step non-fatal with the right index state on an injected failure (one per module); the pack size of the whole store (tar.gz bytes) with the new parts; the per-page and per-click sizes gzip that part B2 will fetch (a c/ tile, an sd/ file, a g/ file, a j/ tile, the largest j/e/ file, the town page HTML) against the 650 KB view budget; the release-asset shape of the climate aggregates and how the job fetches it. Report the measured table and any step that cannot fit the budget with the fix.` },
]

const OWNERSHIP = {
  products: ['website/joins.py', 'tests/test_joins.py', 'website/data/hail-fixture/', 'website/stations.py', 'website/gauges.py', 'tests/test_stations.py', 'tests/test_gauges.py'],
  summary: ['website/summary.py', 'tests/test_summary.py'],
  site: ['website/build.py', 'website/sources.py', 'website/templates/', 'tests/test_site.py', 'tools/smoke_pages.py'],
  docs: ['docs/', 'README.md', 'AGENTS.md', 'research/hail-history/validation-evidence/b5-verification.json', '.github/workflows/hail-store.yml'],
}
function ownerOf(file) {
  for (const [k, prefixes] of Object.entries(OWNERSHIP)) if (prefixes.some((p) => file.startsWith(p) || file.includes(p))) return k
  return 'supervisor'
}

phase('Build')
const builds = await parallel([
  () => agent(PRODUCTS2, { label: 'build:products', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(SUMMARY, { label: 'build:summary', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(SITE, { label: 'build:site-python', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
  () => agent(DOCS, { label: 'build:docs-job', phase: 'Build', model: WORKER }),
])
const [productsR, summaryR, siteR, docsR] = builds
log(`builders done: ${builds.map((b) => (b ? 'ok' : 'none')).join(', ')}`)

phase('Review')
const reports = `Builder reports for context (claims to check, not facts):\nPRODUCTS: ${(productsR || 'none').slice(0, 4000)}\nSUMMARY: ${(summaryR || 'none').slice(0, 4000)}\nSITE: ${(siteR || 'none').slice(0, 4000)}\nDOCS: ${(docsR || 'none').slice(0, 2000)}`
const reviews = await pipeline(
  REVIEWERS,
  (r) => agent(`${r.prompt}\n\n${reports}`, { label: `review:${r.key}`, phase: 'Review', model: WORKER, schema: FINDINGS }).then((result) => ({ r, result })),
  async ({ r, result }) => {
    if (!result) return { key: r.key, findings: [], gates: [], measurements: {}, summary: 'no result' }
    const fs = result.findings.map((f, i) => ({ ...f, id: `${r.key}-${i + 1}` }))
    const verdicts = await parallel(fs.map((f) => () =>
      agent(`Skeptic in ${WT} (branch claude/hail-b5; read-only; scratch only under ${OUT}/skeptic-${f.id}/; never edit, stage, commit or push; never delete outside your folder; disk is tight: no store copies, read ${OUT}/b1/store). Read the parts of ${BRIEF} the finding touches (rules D1 to D30, the store files, the words, the gates, the part B split). A finding is a defect if the code, the store, the pages or the words behave as the finding says and that behaviour breaks a rule of the brief, a repository rule (AGENTS.md: evidence honesty, feed contracts, Python first, tests with every behaviour change, plain wording) or the north star (a cell without its unit or kind word; a zero for missing; a sentence that needs decoding). Reproduce it yourself (run the code, read the store file, render the page, count). Set defect_real true when the defect exists, even if the finding's framing, severity or fix is wrong; set refuted true only when the behaviour does not occur or is allowed by the brief or a decision you cite. Judge the fix: fix_ok, or an adjusted_fix.\n\nFinding ${f.id} (${f.severity}): ${f.file}:${f.line}. Claim: ${f.claim}. Evidence: ${f.evidence}. Proposed fix: ${f.fix}`, { label: `verify:${f.id}`, phase: 'Verify', model: WORKER, schema: VERDICT })))
    return { key: r.key, findings: fs.map((f, i) => ({ ...f, verdict: verdicts[i] || { id: f.id, defect_real: true, refuted: false, severity: f.severity, reason: 'no verdict', fix_ok: true, adjusted_fix: '' } })), gates: result.gates, measurements: result.measurements, summary: result.summary }
  }
)
const all = reviews.filter(Boolean).flatMap((r) => r.findings)
const confirmed = all.filter((f) => f.verdict.defect_real && !f.verdict.refuted).map((f) => ({ id: f.id, file: f.file, line: f.line, claim: f.claim, evidence: f.evidence, severity: f.verdict.severity || f.severity, fix: f.verdict.fix_ok ? f.fix : (f.verdict.adjusted_fix || f.fix), owner: ownerOf(f.file) }))
const refuted = all.filter((f) => !f.verdict.defect_real || f.verdict.refuted).map((f) => ({ id: f.id, file: f.file, claim: f.claim, reason: f.verdict.reason }))
log(`confirmed ${confirmed.length} (blocking ${confirmed.filter((f) => f.severity === 'blocking').length}), refuted ${refuted.length}`)

phase('Fix')
const FIX_DECISIONS = `SUPERVISOR DECISIONS: the brief ${BRIEF} carries decisions D1 to D30 and any later numbered decisions; read them in full before applying any finding and apply the findings in their light (a finding that asks for a choice is decided there; a finding that contradicts a decision is skipped with the decision cited).`
const groups = ['products', 'summary', 'site', 'docs'].map((k) => ({ k, items: confirmed.filter((f) => f.owner === k) })).filter((g) => g.items.length)
const fixReports = await parallel(groups.map((g) => () =>
  agent(`${COMMON}\n\n${FIX_DECISIONS}\n\nYou are the ${g.k} fixer; you own ${OWNERSHIP[g.k].join(', ')}. Apply these confirmed findings exactly (the adjusted fix where given), add or update a test for each behaviour change, run the test modules of your files (quote the tail), and for a store change rebuild the affected part into ${OUT}/b1/store in place only if the products builder's store-ready record says the part is yours; otherwise rebuild into your scratch and compare. Findings:\n${g.items.map((f) => `- ${f.id} [${f.severity}] ${f.file}:${f.line}: ${f.claim}. Fix: ${f.fix}`).join('\n')}\n\nReport each finding as applied, already fixed or skipped with the reason.`, { label: `fix:${g.k}`, phase: 'Fix', model: WORKER })))
